findings.oracle: Real input: live Anthropic /v1/models via AnthropicProvider plus a real-but-invalid sk-ant key. Independent oracle: Anthropic's published catalogue scheme (every id is claude-*, opus/sonnet/haiku families present, API-supplied display names start with 'Claude') and the provider's own _MSG_* / _build_model_info contract. Assertions now back it: claude-* prefix on every id, all three families present, full ModelInfo contract per model (provider==ANTHROPIC, context_window==200000, supports_tools/vision/streaming True), stable paginated id set across two listings, and exact AuthenticationError('API key required'/'Invalid API key') + ProviderError('Not connected') strings on the credential-rejection/not-connected paths that run unconditionally with no key. test_invalid_key drives the real connect() live probe and asserts the normalized contract message, so a removed probe or dropped capability flag goes RED.

Real input: a real compiled JSON template staged on disk and a malformed JSON file; remove driven by name. Independent oracle: the live intellicrack_hexcore HexDocument registry (list_templates before/after) and the documented notification contract. No QFileDialog/QMessageBox monkeypatch: import goes through _import_template_from_path(real path) and remove through _remove_template_named(name); the modal QMessageBox is replaced by a dependency-injected UserNotificationRecorder. Assertions: imported template appears in the real registry with exact TEMPLATE_REGISTERED payload {'template_name':'IMPORTED_HDR'}; malformed import leaves registry unchanged and emits exactly one ('Import Template', 'warning') notification starting 'Import failed:'; remove drops the name from the real registry and emits TEMPLATE_REMOVED {'template_name':'DROPME'}.

Real input: real .hexpat DSL source and real HexPatCompiler output applied to a live HexDocument whose first six bytes are 0x5A4D/0xDEADBEEF. Independent oracle: the real HexPatInterpreter / HexDocument engine decoding exactly two top-level struct fields, derivable from the two-field source. No hexpat_interpreter_available / HexPatInterpreter_cls monkeypatch: the compile branch runs through _on_pattern_apply with real compiled JSON and the interpreter branch through _apply_via_interpreter / _on_pattern_apply with real inline source. Assertions: compile branch registers COMPILEDHDR on the real document and emits TEMPLATE_REGISTERED + PATTERN_EXECUTED {'pattern_name':'COMPILEDHDR','field_count':2}; interpreter branch leaves the document registry untouched yet emits TEMPLATE_REGISTERED {'template_name':'<inline>'} + PATTERN_EXECUTED {'pattern_name':'<inline>','field_count':2}; distinct audit-source loop guards verified by source-bound recorders self-suppressing their own echoes.
